ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (black/dark grey) pixels comprising roughly 92% of the visible surface, punctuated by high-intensity (white) linear and point-source pixel clusters.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Solid dark pigmentation base across both lobes; high-contrast white linear filaments concentrated in the upper-left quadrant and central-right lobe; discrete white point clusters on the far-left lateral margin.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, narrow U-shaped indentation with a calculated convergence angle of approximately 38 degrees at the vertex.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Highly irregular and jagged trailing edge characterized by high-frequency, varying-amplitude peaks and valleys; several deep, rounded notches (indentations) exceeding 15 pixels in depth are visible along the distal edges of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Bilateral convex curves extending outward from the median notch toward the lateral tips; the left lobe displays a steeper upward trajectory compared to the right lobe's more horizontal orientation.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Several circular, high-contrast white clusters (ranging from 4-10 pixels in diameter) localized on the outer-left margin and the upper-right surface, indicating sessile organism attachment sites.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Extensive network of white, non-parallel linear pixel disruptions (rake marks); most prominent cluster consists of vertical and diagonal strikes on the upper-left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Significant cumulative physical scarring manifested as light-colored rake marks and parasitic attachment scars; irregular, ragged trailing edge suggests significant mechanical wear or previous predation attempts.
other_distinctive_markers: A prominent, white, hook-shaped linear mark is visible in the upper-medial region of the left lobe.
